results.fact: Elevation/location of the route's rock-chimney crux
results.evidence: A single trip report (surfaced only in a search summary; the page itself could not be fetched) describes an eroded ~5 ft rock chimney at about 5,100 ft needing 2-3 downclimb moves, which would put it on the climbers' path between Melakwa Lake and Point 5700, not at the summit; a Mountaineers report calls a brief chimney the crux without an elevation. Other sources use 'chimney' for the summit gully (noahzadventures) or a steep downclimb just off the summit (eileensadventures), and WTA, Wikipedia and a 2021 trip report mention no chimney at all. No two sources agree on where the chimney is, so no patch. The row also disagrees internally: turnaround and detailed_rack call it the 'summit chimney' while beta/rope_note put it near 5,100 ft.

results.fact: Avalanche hazard on the route (AVALANCHE panel says N/A, KNOWN HAZARDS/climate say otherwise)
results.correct_value: No avalanche concern once the route has melted out (usually by July); while snow lies on the west flank, Katwalk traverse and summit gullies it is avalanche terrain in the NWAC Snoqualmie Pass zone
results.evidence: NWAC has recorded avalanches on the west face of Kendall Peak (the flank the PCT traverses below) and investigated a 2015 avalanche fatality on Kendall Peak; a WTA June trip report describes ~50-degree snow slopes with long runouts near the Katwalk, and the Mountaineers treat the Kendall area as winter avalanche terrain. The row's own season (Jun-Oct) and access notes put June inside the climbing season, yet the panel's zone text claimed the route is only climbed July-October and that the NWAC zone does not cover it.

patches.fact: Avalanche hazard on the route (AVALANCHE panel says N/A, KNOWN HAZARDS/climate say otherwise)
patches.expect: N/A - non-glaciated route climbed July-October outside the winter avalanche season; the Snoqualmie Pass NWAC zone covers nearby winter backcountry ski/couloir objectives (e.g. the Kendall Adventure Zone), not this summer scramble
patches.value: N/A once the route has melted out, usually by July. While snow still lies on the Katwalk traverse and in the summit gullies (winter, spring, and into June or early July in heavy years), the west flank above and below the PCT is avalanche terrain covered by the NWAC Snoqualmie Pass zone.

results.fact: Mileage along the PCT to the stump/boot-path turnoff (4.6-5 mi vs 5.5-6 mi vs mile 5.75)
results.evidence: beta and pitch_detail put the turnoff at about 4.6-5 mi one-way (consistent with the 9.2 mi round trip), while approach and approach_variants place the switchbacks/stump at ~5.5-6 mi and the itinerary says mile 5.75; partner_requirements says ~11 mi round trip. results.fact: Which side of the peak the route climbs from the gap (east ridge/face vs southwest slopes 'staying left of the broad west ridge')
results.evidence: descent, itinerary day 2 and its schedule, and the timing note say the route follows the east ridge/face from the gap, and Wikipedia names the East Ridge as the easiest route; but approach, climbing_route[0] and approach_variants[0].baseFinding say to ascend the southwest side staying west/south of the broad west ridge, the far side of the peak from a gap that lies east of it, and the route is named Southwest Slopes. No source found describes a southwest-slopes line from the gap, and rewriting the route description needs more than one source, so no patch.

results.fact: which side of the summit the final slopes face (north vs south)
results.correct_value: The standard line climbs the gentle north-facing slopes from the Upper Enchantment basin; the south side drops precipitously
results.evidence: Wenatchee Outdoors says the northern slopes are a nice hike or ski tour from the Upper Enchantment Lakes while the southern slope drops precipitously toward the Nightmare and Knitting Needles. Wikipedia describes the peak's gentle north slope (holding the Snow Creek Glacier remnant). The row's pins agree: the basin and the base-of-slopes junction lie north of the summit, and the row's hazards/watch_out/bail all put the cliffs on the south edge.
